name: Inverse of a two by two matrix
subject: linear_algebra

conditions: A has first row (a,b) and second row (c,d); determinant ad-bc is nonzero; real or complex entries.

evidence: Multiply A by the matrix with rows (d,-b) and (-c,a). The diagonal entries are ad-bc, and both off-diagonal entries vanish by scalar commutativity. Multiplication in the reverse order gives the same result. Dividing by the nonzero determinant gives the identity matrix on both sides.
Reference cross-check: https://openstax.org/books/college-algebra-2e/pages/7-7-solving-systems-with-inverses. Checked 2026-11-27. Proposed maintainer approval; not independent human certification.
